trust_decision.summary: After any failed unpack the streaming parser context must be returned to a clean state: unpack_clear must release every stack slot (i = 0 .. top-1), the map_key whose reference unpack_callback_map_item already consumed must be nulled, and unpack_init must re-establish cs/trail/top so a reused Unpacker cannot decref or read a stale stack entry.

landing_point.why: The report says 'Unpacker reuse after a caught error', so an engineer goes to the Python-level _unpack handler where the exception is raised and where a reset would be obvious; the root cause is one layer down in the C template.

fix_sites.entry_point: msgpack.unpackb() failure path, Unpacker.__init__ re-initialisation, Unpacker.__dealloc__ (all call unpack_clear)
fix_sites.module_kind: C template header, low-level parser API
C template header, low-level parser API
C template header, low-level parser API

O3_reason_to_dismiss: unpack_template.h is internal C machinery whose unpack_clear already carries the #671/#687 leak-fix comment, so a solver can argue the report's crash is a Python-level misuse problem that a reset in _unpack fixes, and that the map_key = NULL line belongs to the earlier leak fixes rather than to this use-after-free.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Incomplete input must NOT reset the parser: on ret == 0 the cs/trail/top state has to survive so feed()/file_like can continue a partially parsed object, and unpack_init may only run after a completed object (ret == 1). A fix that clears on every non-1 return breaks streaming and the file_like path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the pure-Python _unpack/Unpacker that mirrors the C parser but never restores _buff_i after a hook raises
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: fallback.py is the same public API for MSGPACK_PUREPYTHON/pypy builds, so a maintainer fixing recovery semantics would naturally write the twin there; it cannot segfault, so it is a decoy rather than a required site.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second producer of ctx->stack[0].obj that assigns the root without releasing the previous root object
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: read_array_header/read_map_header write the root slot outside unpack_execute, so a maintainer clearing the context on error could easily forget this route.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: unpack_callback_map_item returns -1 on a strict_map_key failure without dropping k and v, another ownership site next to the same sink
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the refcount handoff in this callback is exactly the kind of code a maintainer would touch while fixing the map_key lifetime.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a lifecycle reset site (__dealloc__/__init__) that a maintainer would implement separately from the per-call error path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: both already call unpack_clear, which is why the same mechanism reappears on destruction and re-initialisation.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add unpack_clear(&self.ctx) / unpack_init in _unpack's error path in msgpack/_unpacker.pyx and stop there, leaving unpack_clear's i = 1 loop and the map_key handoff in msgpack/unpack_template.h untouched.
